solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eagerly grab short sleep in first half of meal

indicators.note: the short sleep sits in the middle of the shortened meal, cut open by it
only the opening three of the six letters of the evening meal are kept

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone hungrily seizes a quick doze halfway through dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The meal is supper, and 'first half of' means its letters are halved before the doze goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap something up is an idiom for seizing it quickly and eagerly before others can.

clue.text: Writer was wounded, bitten

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, so it stands in for a writer
bled means lost blood, as one does when wounded

explanation.surface: An author got hurt and was bitten.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbled means bitten gently in small mouthfuls, a close synonym.

clue.text: Run from street having been nipped by bird

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is caught between the bird's letters as if pinched

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Someone flees down a road after being pecked by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE, a crossword favourite for the magpie, nips ST to give PI-ST-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a ski run, a prepared slope for skiing down.

clue.text: Eye-catching concert in part of St Mary's, Paddington?

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
taken as written
ENT (ear, nose and throat) is a department of a hospital such as St Mary's in Paddington, London

explanation.surface: A notable musical event takes place inside a London church or building.
explanation.walkthrough: St Mary's, Paddington is a London hospital, not a church, so its 'part' is a department: ENT, ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent stands out and catches the eye, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Vehicles with various escorts going round roundabout

indicators.note: the rearranged letters circle the ring-shaped letter, enclosing it
various suggests the letters of escorts appear in a different arrangement

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Cars with a mixture of escorts circle a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' turns ESCORTS into SCOTERS, and 'going round' wraps it about O to give SCOOTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooters are small motor or kick vehicles, so they are examples of vehicles.

clue.text: Put backside on article that's pleasant, not totally bad

parts.note: to put one's backside down is to sit, past tense sat
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped from the synonym, leaving it incomplete

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone sat down on a pleasant item that was not entirely bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' shortens NICE to NIC: SAT + A + NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, utterly evil, an intensified sense of bad.

clue.text: Waste material out from Cornish river

parts.note: out from, as in made out of, means of: born of, out from
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: Rubbish is being carried out of a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a butchered animal, once regarded as waste.

clue.text: One escaping from a time immersed in river — medical care needed

indicators.note: the shortened phrase is plunged inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in England
taken as written

indicators.note: the numeral one leaves the phrase, being removed from it

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone fell into a river and needs a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the Roman numeral I; 'escaping from' removes it from the two words before 'immersed in' sinks what is left into the river. The Trent flows through the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the care a doctor gives a patient, the medical sense of the word.

clue.text: You'll see me in trade after butchering

definitions.text: You'll see me in trade after butchering

indicators.note: butchering means cutting up, so the letters are chopped and reassembled

explanation.surface: A piece of beef speaks: you'll find me sold once I've been cut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after butchering' scrambles the two words; read whole, the clue is the meat itself talking about where it is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Red meat such as beef or lamb is what a butcher sells after cutting up a carcass.

clue.text: How strife is re-enacted within well-marked battle site

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit inside the word for clearly marked

parts.note: bold type is heavy and well-marked

indicators.note: re-enacting puts the letters through a new performance, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Historical battle re-enactors stage a fight at a famous field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is re-enacted' gives SWORTHFIE, which 'within' sets in the bold type. Bosworth Field, Leicestershire, is where Richard III died in 1485.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosworth Field is the English site of the 1485 battle that ended the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: African man embracing one of the Spice Girls

indicators.note: the man's name hugs the singer's name, holding it inside

parts.note: Alan is a man's name
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the pop group

explanation.surface: A man from Africa hugs a famous pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: AL-GERI-AN: Geri Halliwell was a member of the 1990s British pop group the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algerian is a person from Algeria in North Africa, so an African.

clue.text: Maybe I allowed Cockney woman to be heard

indicators.note: said aloud, the words for permitted and a Londoner's dropped-h her run together

parts.note: allowed is let, and a Cockney woman is 'er, her with the h dropped, giving let 'er

explanation.surface: Perhaps I let a London woman speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, speakers of the traditional East London accent, drop initial h, so 'let her' becomes 'let 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: I is a character of the alphabet, an example of the item in question, signalled by Maybe.

clue.text: Quote from a theologian attached to university church

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A citation from a theology scholar connected with a college chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite or put forward as evidence, so it is to quote.

clue.text: Rental due to be changed or left alone?

indicators.note: changing the letters means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: Is the rent owed to be revised, or kept as it is?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' rearranges RENTAL DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left alone stays unaltered, unchanged in any way, a synonym.

clue.text: Litter left after the match?

parts.note: match suggests a football game and its rubbish, but it is a wedding match, where paper shreds are thrown over the couple

explanation.surface: Rubbish strewn about once a football game has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Match here is a marriage, not a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti, the paper scraps thrown at a wedding, lies scattered as rubbish afterwards.

clue.text: Black attire torn with anger?

indicators.note: torn suggests the words are ripped apart and remade

explanation.surface: Dark clothing ripped in a fit of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' rearranges WITH ANGER; the definition reads cryptically as clothes for the black of night.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the black part of the day, and wear means attire, so this is clothing for bedtime.

clue.text: Irish priest outside game joining worker gone off naughtily

indicators.note: the priest's name sits outside the other two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: Father Ted is the Irish priest of the TV sitcom
RU is rugby union
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A cleric surrounds a game with a labourer who has wandered off mischievously.
explanation.walkthrough: The priest is from Father Ted, a TV sitcom about Irish clergy; 'outside' wraps him round the game and worker, and 'joining' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Truanted means stayed away from school without permission, slipping off naughtily.

clue.text: Like the value of property Arab let out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A property is rented out by an Arab owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ARAB LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratable value is the assessed worth of property on which local rates are charged.

clue.text: A US lawyer keeps quiet in study, showing no emotion

indicators.note: the lawyer group sits inside the room, cutting it open

parts.note: a den is a private study

indicators.note: the lawyer holds the quiet letter inside

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
p, piano, is the musical sign for quiet

explanation.surface: An American lawyer stays silent in a study with a blank face.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, district attorney, is a US prosecutor; 'keeps' and 'in' nest the pieces two deep, giving the inner run ADPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan look is expressionless and shows nothing of the feelings behind it.

clue.text: After game, one of the nobs fell asleep

indicators.note: the posh person's word follows the board game in the answer

parts.note: go is an ancient board game
a toff is a British upper-class person, one of the nobs

explanation.surface: Following a match, a posh gent nodded off.
explanation.walkthrough: Toff and nob are British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off, or drop off, to sleep is an informal idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Female vocalists heading off — they may be wearing rings

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the word is removed

parts.note: singers are vocalists

explanation.surface: Women singers leaving, perhaps adorned with jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes only the first letter of the vocalists, leaving INGERS; the definition plays on rings as jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are the digits on which rings are worn, so they may wear rings.

clue.text: Position of monuments — not far side of square

indicators.note: not means the chosen letter is left out of the word

parts.note: statues are monuments

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Where statues stand, away from the edge of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far side of' square is E, which 'not' removes from STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means standing or rank, a person's position in society.

clue.text: Part of plant absorbing a liquid when it's hot

indicators.note: the stalk takes the letter inside it, as a plant soaks up water

parts.note: the stem is part of a plant

explanation.surface: A plant's stalk takes up water on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Water heated to boiling turns to vapour, so this is a liquid in its hot form.

clue.text: Athenian at home in any element

indicators.note: being at home in something means being inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Timon of Athens is the Shakespeare title character

explanation.surface: A citizen of Athens feels comfortable in any substance.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMON, from Shakespeare's Timon of Athens, is 'at home in' ANY: AN-TIMON-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a chemical element, symbol Sb, a brittle metalloid.

clue.text: Agency to provide statistical data

definitions.meaning: the agency or method by which something is done
averages from a data set, in the plural of the statistical term

explanation.surface: An organisation set up to supply figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a method by which something is achieved and averages in statistics.

clue.text: Noble work

parts.note: work reads as labour of noble character, but it is a reference book about the aristocracy

explanation.surface: A virtuous effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Noble means aristocrat, not virtuous: this is the famous British guide to the peerage, the titled nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: This British reference book lists the nobility and their lineages, so it is a work on nobles.

clue.text: Country driver

parts.note: suggests a motorist on rural roads, but means someone who drives animals in the countryside

explanation.surface: A motorist on rural lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: Driver here is someone who drives cattle, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman tends and drives livestock in rural areas, a drover of the countryside.

clue.text: Refuse is collected in quiet interval

indicators.note: the small word is gathered up inside the pause

parts.note: a rest is a quiet interval, as in music

explanation.surface: Rubbish is picked up during a calm break.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to refuse to comply or give way, a verb synonym.
